actions.reason: In BasicTokenizer.train, delay allocating and filling the merged id list until the first occurrence of the selected pair is found, copying the unchanged prefix with a slice and then scanning the remainder. The selected pair comes from the current adjacent-pair counts, so the resulting ids and merges are unchanged while reducing per-element append work in the merge pass.

diff --git a/minbpe/basic.py b/minbpe/basic.py
--- a/minbpe/basic.py
+++ b/minbpe/basic.py
@@ -39,19 +39,28 @@ class BasicTokenizer(Tokenizer):
             # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
             idx = 256 + i
             # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
-            newids = []
-            append = newids.append
             p0, p1 = pair
             j = 0
             n = len(ids)
-            while j < n:
-                if ids[j] == p0 and j < n - 1 and ids[j+1] == p1:
+            last = n - 1
+            while j < last:
+                if ids[j] == p0 and ids[j+1] == p1:
+                    newids = ids[:j]
+                    append = newids.append
                     append(idx)
                     j += 2
-                else:
-                    append(ids[j])
-                    j += 1
-            ids = newids
+                    while j < last:
+                        if ids[j] == p0 and ids[j+1] == p1:
+                            append(idx)
+                            j += 2
+                        else:
+                            append(ids[j])
+                            j += 1
+                    if j == last:
+                        append(ids[j])
+                    ids = newids
+                    break
+                j += 1
             # save the merge
             merges[pair] = idx
             vocab[idx] = vocab[pair[0]] + vocab[pair[1]]

Changed minbpe/basic.py in BasicTokenizer.train. Tried three merge-loop shapes. The last one delayed allocation of ids until the selected pair was first seen, copied the unchanged prefix with a slice, then scanned the rest.

The useful part is avoiding per-element append work before the first selected pair in BasicTokenizer.train. The earlier forms did not help. The selected pair comes from current adjacent-pair counts, so the ids and merges stayed unchanged in sandbox.
